title: Text Editor
description: Build a text editor with cursor movement, character insertion/deletion, text statistics, and undo functionality.

steps.title: Create document state with content and cursor
steps.description: Define a `document` object with `content` (string) and `cursorPosition` (number, zero-based index). Initialize with some sample text and log the state.
hints: Cursor position represents the index where the next character will be inserted
Log the document state: 'Content: <content>, Cursor at <position>'

verification.successMessage: Document state is initialized with content and cursor position!
verification.failureMessage: Create a doc object with content 'Hello world' and cursorPosition set to 5.

steps.title: Implement insertChar function
steps.description: Write an `insertChar` function that takes a character and inserts it at the current cursor position, incrementing the cursor by 1. Log the updated content.
hints: Split content at cursor: content.slice(0, pos) + char + content.slice(pos)
Or convert to array, splice, and join

verification.successMessage: Characters insert correctly at the cursor position!
verification.failureMessage: insertChar('l') should change 'Helo' to 'Hello' and advance cursor from 3 to 4.

steps.title: Implement deleteChar function
steps.description: Write a `deleteChar` function that deletes the character just before the cursor (backspace). Decrement the cursor by 1 after deletion. Log the updated content.

verification.successMessage: Backspace deletes the character before the cursor!
verification.failureMessage: deleteChar() with cursor at 5 should remove 'o', changing 'Hello world' to 'Hell world' and cursor to 4.

steps.title: Implement cursor movement
steps.description: Write `moveCursorLeft`, `moveCursorRight`, `moveCursorHome`, and `moveCursorEnd` functions. Log the cursor position after each movement.

verification.successMessage: All cursor movement functions work correctly!
verification.failureMessage: From cursor 5: Left should be 4, Right back to 5, Home to 0, End to 11.

steps.title: Calculate text statistics
steps.description: Write `getWordCount` and `getCharCount` functions. `getCharCount` returns total characters (excluding spaces). `getWordCount` returns word count. Log both statistics.
hints: getWordCount: content.split(/\s+/).filter(w => w !== '').length or split and count

verification.successMessage: Text statistics calculate correct character and word counts!
verification.failureMessage: getCharCount should return 19 (23 chars - 4 spaces). getWordCount should return 5.

steps.title: Implement undo stack
steps.description: Create an `undoStack` array and modify `insertChar` and `deleteChar` to save state snapshots before each operation. Write an `undo` function that restores the previous state.
hints: Save snapshot before change: undoStack.push({ content: doc.content, cursorPosition: doc.cursorPosition })
Undo: pop the last state and restore it: Object.assign(doc, undoStack.pop())
Clear the current state reference when pushing

codeTemplate.python:
doc = {"content": "Hi", "cursorPosition": 2}
undoStack = []

def saveState():
  undoStack.append({"content": doc["content"], "cursorPosition": doc["cursorPosition"]})

def insertChar(char):
  saveState()
  doc["content"] = doc["content"][:doc["cursorPosition"]] + char + doc["content"][doc["cursorPosition"]:]
  doc["cursorPosition"] += 1

def deleteChar():
  if doc["cursorPosition"] > 0:
    saveState()
    doc["content"] = doc["content"][:doc["cursorPosition"] - 1] + doc["content"][doc["cursorPosition"]:]
    doc["cursorPosition"] -= 1

def undo():
  

insertChar("!")
print("After insert:", doc["content"])
insertChar("?")
print("After insert:", doc["content"])
undo()
print("After undo:", doc["content"])
undo()
print("After undo:", doc["content"])

verification.test: output.includes('After insert: Hi!?') && output.includes('After undo: Hi!') && output.includes('After undo: Hi')
verification.successMessage: Undo stack correctly reverts document state!
verification.failureMessage: After inserting '!' then '?', undo should go back to 'Hi!', then undo again to 'Hi'.
